question: Who converted Menander to Buddhism?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Nagasena**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Buddhist monk **Nagasena converted the Indo-Greek king Menander to Buddhism**.
 
• The conversation between the two is recorded in the book **Milinda Panho, which translates to "Questions of Milinda". **
 
• ​Menander was **an Indo-Greek ruler **who ruled over India. He was also known as Milinda. 
 
• **Nagasena was a holy man** and Buddhist sage. 
 
• The conversation between Menander and Nagasena** took place in Sagala,** which is present-day Sialkot. 
 
• The book Milinda Panho is** written in Pali and was written in 130 BC. **
 
• **The book is considered canonical in Burmese Buddhism. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__ **

 Key Facts
 
 

 
 Bhadrabahu
 
 - One of the last great Acharyas (teachers) of Jainism in ancient India.
 
 

 - Led the Jain community after the death of Chandragupta Maurya.
 
 

 - Famous for his role in the spread of Jainism, especially in southern India.
 
 

 - He is believed to have taken a group of Jain followers to South India to preserve the Jain traditions.
 
 

 
 Buddhaghosh
 
 - Famous for translating many important Buddhist texts from Sanskrit to Pali.
 
 

 - His most notable work is the "Visuddhimagga" (Path of Purification), a comprehensive manual on Theravada Buddhism.
 
 

 - His works were instrumental in shaping the Theravada Buddhist tradition.
 
 

 
 Asvaghosha
 
 - A major figure in the early history of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
 

 - Known for writing "Buddhacharita", an epic poem that narrates the life of Lord Buddha.
 
 

 - Played a significant role in promoting Mahayana Buddhist ideas and in the development of Buddhist philosophy and literature.
